subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce tool-result-backed verification, fail-closed diagnostics, or documented non-verification when visible final text claims side effects?
rationale: Current code deliberately supports automatic final delivery and message-tool-only suppression, while generic claim verification was previously closed as plugin scope; choosing core verification, fallback, warning, or documentation changes channel UX, privacy, and compatibility semantics.

options.title: Define core verification policy
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved tool-result ledger or diagnostic before delivering visible success claims for side-effecting actions on Telegram/ACP source turns.

options.title: Limit scope to delivery-tool gaps
options.body: Treat missing source delivery when the message tool is omitted as the platform-owned class and leave broader side-effect verification to prompts, hooks, or plugins.

options.title: Document current boundary
options.body: Document that OpenClaw transports model final text and does not verify arbitrary claimed side effects without a future plugin or hook policy.

recommendation.title: Define core verification policy
recommendation.body: Require a maintainer-approved tool-result ledger or diagnostic before delivering visible success claims for side-effecting actions on Telegram/ACP source turns.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a source-reply delivery and privacy policy choice, and steipete merged the closest warning-only policy change.
